official.description_text:
Postdoc in Robot Learning for Manipulation
Login and apply
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Job description
The postdoctoral researcher will work on robot learning for manipulation, exploring state-of-the-art Vision–Language–Action (VLA) models for tabletop, mobile, or dexterous manipulation. A key focus is leveraging whole-body motion and/or dexterous, multi-fingered hands to improve perception and control, enabling robots to solve complex, contact-rich tasks that require coordinated base, arm, and hand behaviors in dynamic environments. We seek candidates with a strong background in robotics and machine learning, and demonstrated experience in at least two of the following areas: deep learning, reinforcement learning, imitation learning, robot perception, navigation, grasping, and dexterous or mobile manipulation. Experience in any of the following is especially valued: whole-body control, humanoid or multi-DOF platforms, multi-fingered hands, tactile sensing, or learning-based manipulation in simulation and/or on real systems.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree. This eligibility requirement must be met no later than the time the employment decision is made.
Research expertise in machine learning/robotics.
Documented strong programming skills.
The candidate should have an outstanding research and publication list.
You have well developed analytical and problem-solving skills.
The candidate should have very good knowledge of the English language, such as written and oral skills since communication is essential of this role.
Preferred qualifications
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree, obtained within the last three years prior to the application deadline
You have good pedagogical ability.
Awareness of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality.
You are independent in your work and have no problem collaborating with others.
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH.

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system to apply for this position. You are responsible for ensuring that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Maximally two pages long.
Your complete application must be received at KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).

ai.summary: Postdoctoral position at KTH Royal Institute of Technology focused on robot learning for manipulation using Vision–Language–Action (VLA) models for tabletop, mobile, and dexterous manipulation tasks. Research emphasizes deep learning, reinforcement learning, and coordinated multi-limb robotic control in contact-rich environments.

thematic_fit.rationale: The position is primarily a machine learning and robotics control problem: learning-based manipulation, VLA models, deep reinforcement learning, and multi-DOF control systems. While the researcher has worked with immersive environments and multiplayer systems, the core research question here concerns robotic perception, dexterous motor control, and policy learning—not human-computer interaction, spatial cognition, or learning outcomes. The robots are autonomous agents, not tools for studying human behavior. No thematic overlap exists with the researcher's target identity.

methodological_fit.rationale: Both involve interaction design at scale (multiplayer systems vs. multi-limb robots), but the evaluation frameworks diverge. The researcher evaluates human spatial learning and wayfinding transfer; this position evaluates robot task success via simulation and real-world metrics (grasping success, trajectory accuracy). The researcher's user study methodology and human factors approach do not transfer. Machine learning model validation (training curves, sim-to-real transfer) is orthogonal to HCI evaluation. The researcher would need deep learning, RL, and robotics simulation expertise.

growth_value.rationale: The position has minor adjacent value only. Exposure to embodied AI and multi-agent systems might inform future work on AI-augmented immersive environments, but the researcher would be investing 2 years in deep learning and robotics control—skills not directly applicable to human-centred spatial cognition research. This is not a strategic stepping stone to the target identity; it is a detour into machine learning and robotics. However, it is closer to XR/immersive systems than the power systems or structural positions, which gives it modest credibility as exploratory adjacent work.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH is a respected technical university with strong robotics and AI groups. Prof. Danica Kragic Jensfelt is a well-known roboticist with an established publication record. However, this position is machine learning / robotics engineering, not human-centred interaction research. The group is not aligned with target institutions' HCI or human-centred XR researchers. Two years here might raise the researcher's profile in robotics circles but would not strengthen credentials in human-centred immersive systems or spatial cognition communities. The position type (postdoc) is appropriate, but the domain direction is wrong.

eligibility_flags: Position requires PhD in robotics or machine learning obtained within 3 years of application deadline (late Nov 2026). Researcher is completing MSc by Research, not PhD. Ineligible unless defended by that date.

Posting emphasizes 'strong background in robotics and machine learning' and 'demonstrated experience in at least two of: deep learning, reinforcement learning, imitation learning, robot perception, navigation, grasping.' Researcher's background is HCI and XR; no ML/RL experience stated.

Outstanding research and publication list required. Researcher has 1 first-author journal article and 1 in-progress mapping review—acceptable early-career record, but not yet the publication density typical of competitive postdoc applicants in ML/robotics.
risks: Hard eligibility barrier: Must hold PhD by application deadline (late Nov 2026). If researcher is still in thesis stage, application is ineligible.

Competitiveness risk: ML/robotics postdoc positions at KTH attract candidates with deep learning, RL, or robot learning publications. The researcher's HCI background is not competitive; ML/robotics experts would be ranked higher.

Skill gap: The researcher would require rapid upskilling in deep learning, RL, and robot manipulation—domains not covered by current portfolio. Realistic onboarding time exceeds available ramp-up in a focused 2-year role.
Career direction ambiguity: Pivoting to machine learning robotics signals unclear focus to future reviewers in target HCI/immersive systems communities.
Opportunity cost: Effort on this application (acquiring ML/robotics credentials) diverts from strengthening HCI/spatial cognition narrative for aligned positions.
